subject: Sociology
chapter: Terms, Concepts and their Use in Sociology
central_question: How do precise sociological concepts help us analyse social groups, inequality, status, roles and social control beyond everyday common sense?
in_scope_units: Introduction: why sociology needs precise terms and how concepts reflect different theoretical approaches and the transition from pre-modern to modern society.
Social Groups and Society: aggregates, quasi groups, social groups, social structure and the characteristics of organised collectivities.
Types of Groups: primary and secondary groups, community and association, in-groups and out-groups, reference groups and peer groups.
Social Stratification: structured inequalities, slavery, caste, estate and class, including Marxist, Weberian and functionalist views.
Status and Role: status, role, status set, status sequence, ascribed and achieved status, prestige, role taking, role conflict, role stereotyping and agency.
Society and Social Control: functionalist and conflict views, formal and informal social control, sanctions, norms and deviance.
banned_topics: Detailed study of social institutions such as family, marriage, kinship, religion and education, which belongs to the next chapter.
Full research-method procedures and fieldwork design, which are treated later in the book.
A comprehensive account of caste, class and gender inequality, which the chapter says will be developed in Understanding Society.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any collection of people in one place is a social group.
known_pitfalls.correction: An aggregate or quasi group may lack structure, awareness and persistent interaction; a social group has continuity, shared interests, norms, belonging and a definable structure.

known_pitfalls.claim: Primary groups are always traditional and secondary groups are always modern.
known_pitfalls.correction: The contrast is a useful type, but the chapter warns that a complete contrast is not an accurate description of reality and formal relations may become close over time.

known_pitfalls.claim: Modern class society provides perfect mobility.
known_pitfalls.correction: Although class is more open and achievement-based than caste, sociological studies remain far from the ideal of perfect mobility.

known_pitfalls.claim: A role and a status mean the same thing.
known_pitfalls.correction: Status is a social position with rights and duties; role is the dynamic or behavioural aspect of that status.
The chapter uses Khasi matriliny to show intense role conflict for men and also describes strain experienced by women.

known_pitfalls.claim: Social control is exercised only through law and police.
known_pitfalls.correction: Social control may be formal or informal and includes family, religion, kinship, praise, criticism, ridicule, body language, sanctions and force.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 1 to explain why ordinary familiar words require precise sociological definitions.
Use NCERT Exercise 2 to classify the groups in a student's life sociologically.
Use NCERT Exercise 3 to analyse how stratification structures individual opportunities.
Use NCERT Exercise 5 to map a person's status set, roles and changes over time.
Use NCERT Exercise 4 to compare formal and informal social control in different social spheres.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with an EXERCISES section containing Questions 1–5.
